source.title: Late-Stage Generalization Collapse in Grokking: Detecting anti-grokking with Weightwatcher

record.tranche_reason: The study says it reproduces canonical grokking setups, including modular addition, and reports training and test accuracy through extended training. It extends the training duration to examine late-stage behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper reports grokking and late-stage accuracy trajectories, phase-wise WeightWatcher α measurements, and Fourier-frequency measurements for modular addition. It does not sweep training-set size, directly test removal of memorizing components, or compare optimizer or numerical choices. Its correlation-trap counts are a new diagnostic of late-stage collapse, not a direct measure named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: It reproduces two standard grokking setups: the Nanda-style modular-addition transformer and the Omnigrok-style MNIST MLP with init scaled by 8. It reports train and test accuracy by phase, plus Fourier profiles of the modular-addition embeddings. These bear directly on V1, V2 and V3. Its new result, late-stage 'anti-grokking' collapse, fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors report a third phase, anti-grokking, in both the MNIST MLP and the modular-addition transformer: test accuracy collapses after long training while train accuracy stays perfect. Correlation traps are their primary detector, and average α ≈ 2 at peak grokking is secondary. In the MLP, weight decay suppresses trap onset and the extent of the drop. They also propose that pre-grokking reflects incompletely converged layers.
record.recipe_differences: The paper describes reproducing modular-addition and MNIST grokking setups, but extends training substantially and adds WeightWatcher diagnostics and Fourier analyses. It also studies MNIST with and without weight decay.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with weight decay (0 versus 0.01) and with the globally rescaled alpha-to-4 condition. The paper also reports different modular-addition accuracy summaries in Table 5 and Appendix H.1 Table 8.

fits_no_version.finding: After grokking, prolonged training (~10^7 steps, WD=0) collapses test accuracy while train stays at 1.0. MNIST drops to ~0.5; modular addition drops to 0.68 or 0.60.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokked generalization is not stable: extended training without weight decay can produce a late collapse ('anti-grokking') distinct from ungrokking.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight decay 0.01 limits the late collapse to a slight drop and a near-peak plateau.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay stabilizes post-grokking generalization against late collapse.

fits_no_version.finding: In anti-grok, α falls below 2 (MNIST) or drifts up (modular addition), correlation traps appear, and the embed/unembed Fourier profile goes broadband.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late collapse coincides with spectral correlation traps and loss of a sharp Fourier embedding.

record.problems: The evidence uses a small number of task setups; the MNIST setup specifies random seed 0, while reported phase variability is not consistently detailed. The modular-addition phase summaries differ between Table 5 and Appendix H.1 Table 8. The paper does not sweep dataset size or optimizer/numerical settings, and the rescaled MNIST result has no stated architecture details in its phase table.
record.rows_left_out: No additional accuracy or α results were omitted. Correlation-trap counts and large-language-model layer spectra are discussed in gate_note because they are diagnostics or weight measurements, not outcomes measuring the delayed-generalization or circuit claims in the tested versions.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size; step counts of the delay for modular addition.
Removal of memorizing components; a continuous measure that leads the test jump. Only phase snapshots are given.
Text and molecule data; an init-scale or weight-norm sweep that switches grokking on or off (a lazy-to-rich transition).
All of it. The GPT-OSS α histograms are weight diagnostics, not training trajectories.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size, ungrokking.
All of it; no cross-run algorithm comparison.
No optimizer or numerics manipulation. The MNIST run uses float64 and MSE (no softmax) with AdamW, but this is not compared.

missing.what: ℓ2 weight norm increases throughout WD=0 training yet grokking occurs (Golechha comparison)
missing.locator: Section 1 (Weight Norm Analysis); Appendix B, D; Figure 13

missing.what: Key-bank overlap with the rule-frequency set S rises from 2 of 6 (PRE) to 5 of 6 (GROK); rule-kernel DFT powers rise PRE→GROK
Golechha progress measures (activation sparsity, weight entropy, local circuit complexity) track pre-grok and grok, but no lead time is quantified
Phase boundaries shift earlier under rescaling alpha 4 (grok 5×10^4–5×10^5) vs main run (10^5–10^6)

record.verdict_notes: Table 5 and Table 8 give different modular-addition accuracies (pre-grok 0.40 vs 0.13; grok 0.97 vs 1.0). The MNIST setup scales init by 8 (Omnigrok-style) and uses float64 with MSE loss. Delay therefore occurs without softmax or float32 limits, but the optimizer is AdamW and nothing is varied, so V7 is left untested. GPT-OSS α histograms are not delayed-generalization evidence.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not vary training-set size, so it does not test whether smaller training sets require more optimization. It also does not establish that pre-grokking modular-addition test accuracy is at chance.

The study measures phase-wise α and Fourier profiles, but does not causally identify a generalizing circuit, measure removal of memorizing components, or show that a continuous progress measure anticipates the accuracy jump.
It reports an image-task result and a globally rescaled run, but does not test text or molecule data, a lazy-to-rich transition, or a systematic initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep.
The paper reports layer diagnostics for large language models, but no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning trajectory or delayed-generalization result.
The study compares weight decay settings but does not test whether weight decay selects a more efficient circuit, vary dataset size to find a critical size, or test ungrokking below that size.
It does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs.
It does not control for adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax limits, or test whether those choices produce the delay.
